verses.text: In the twenty-seventh year that Jeroboam was king of Israel, Azariah son of Amaziah began to rule as king of Judah.
He was sixteen years old when he became king, and he ruled in Jerusalem for fifty-two years. His mother was Jecoliah, from Jerusalem.
He did what was right in the LORD's eyes, just as his father Amaziah had done.
But the high places were not removed. The people still offered sacrifices and burned incense there.
The LORD struck the king with leprosy, and he had it until the day he died. He lived in a separate house. His son Jotham was in charge of the palace and ruled the people of the land.
The rest of what Azariah did, and all his deeds, are written in the book of the history of the kings of Judah.
Azariah died and was buried with his ancestors in the city of David. His son Jotham became king after him.
In the thirty-eighth year that Azariah was king of Judah, Zechariah son of Jeroboam became king of Israel in Samaria. He ruled for six months.
He did what was evil in the LORD's eyes, as his ancestors had done. He did not turn away from the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat, who had made Israel sin.
Shallum son of Jabesh made a plot against Zechariah. He attacked him in front of the people, killed him, and became king in his place.
The rest of what Zechariah did is written in the book of the history of the kings of Israel.
So the LORD's promise to Jehu came true: "Your descendants will sit on the throne of Israel for four generations."
Shallum son of Jabesh became king in the thirty-ninth year that Uzziah was king of Judah. He ruled in Samaria for one month.
Then Menahem son of Gadi went up from Tirzah to Samaria. He attacked Shallum son of Jabesh there, killed him, and became king in his place.
The rest of what Shallum did, and the plot he made, are written in the book of the history of the kings of Israel.

At that time Menahem, starting out from Tirzah, attacked the town of Tiphsah, everyone in it, and the area around it. He attacked it because its people would not open their gates to him. He ripped open all the pregnant women there.
In the thirty-ninth year that Azariah was king of Judah, Menahem son of Gadi became king of Israel. He ruled in Samaria for ten years.
He did what was evil in the LORD's eyes. As long as he lived, he did not turn away from the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat, who had made Israel sin.
Then Pul king of Assyria invaded the land. Menahem gave Pul about thirty-four thousand kilograms of silver, so Pul would support him and help him keep control of the kingdom.
Menahem got the money from Israel by forcing every rich man to pay fifty pieces of silver. He gave it to the king of Assyria. So the king of Assyria turned back and did not stay in the land.
The rest of what Menahem did, and all his deeds, are written in the book of the history of the kings of Israel.
Menahem died, and his son Pekahiah became king after him.
In the fiftieth year that Azariah was king of Judah, Pekahiah son of Menahem became king of Israel in Samaria. He ruled for two years.
He did what was evil in the LORD's eyes. He did not turn away from the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat, who had made Israel sin.

Pekah son of Remaliah, one of his chief officers, made a plot against him. With fifty men from Gilead, Pekah attacked Pekahiah in the strongest part of the palace in Samaria. He killed him, along with Argob and Arieh, and became king in his place.
The rest of what Pekahiah did, and all his deeds, are written in the book of the history of the kings of Israel.
In the fifty-second year that Azariah was king of Judah, Pekah son of Remaliah became king of Israel in Samaria. He ruled for twenty years.
He did what was evil in the LORD's eyes. He did not turn away from the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat, who had made Israel sin.

While Pekah was king of Israel, Tiglath-Pileser king of Assyria came and captured Ijon, Abel Beth Maacah, Janoah, Kedesh, Hazor, Gilead, and Galilee, all the land of Naphtali. He took the people away as prisoners to Assyria.
Then Hoshea son of Elah made a plot against Pekah son of Remaliah. He attacked him, killed him, and became king in his place. This was in the twentieth year of Jotham son of Uzziah.
The rest of what Pekah did, and all his deeds, are written in the book of the history of the kings of Israel.
In the second year that Pekah son of Remaliah was king of Israel, Jotham son of Uzziah began to rule as king of Judah.
He was twenty-five years old when he became king, and he ruled in Jerusalem for sixteen years. His mother was Jerusha, the daughter of Zadok.
He did what was right in the LORD's eyes, just as his father Uzziah had done.
But the high places were not removed. The people still offered sacrifices and burned incense there. Jotham built the Upper Gate of the LORD's temple.
The rest of what Jotham did, and all his deeds, are written in the book of the history of the kings of Judah.
In those days the LORD began to send Rezin king of Syria and Pekah son of Remaliah to attack Judah.
Jotham died and was buried with his ancestors in the city of his ancestor David. His son Ahaz became king after him.
